title: Webhook retries created duplicate fulfilment tasks
description: A fictional customer reports that three orders appeared twice in their fulfilment queue after webhook retries. Delivery logs show a timeout followed by a 200 response for the same event ID. It is not yet known whether the receiving service deduplicates events. The first report was at 09:20 UTC; other features appear unaffected.

draft.summary: Repeated delivery of the same event may be associated with duplicate fulfilment processing. The available report does not establish the cause or whether receiver-side deduplication is present.

observations.statement: A timeout was followed by a 200 response for the same event ID, and duplicate tasks were reported.
Webhook retries can repeat an event ID; delivery and business processing must be investigated separately.

checks.action: Compare a redacted event timeline with receiver acknowledgements and fulfilment task IDs.
checks.reason: This can establish whether repeated delivery also caused repeated business processing.

checks.action: Confirm the first observed time, number of affected orders and whether other customers are affected.
checks.reason: Scope is still uncertain and should inform the human priority decision.

missing_information: Does the receiver deduplicate by the stable event ID?
Are any other customers or time periods affected?
draft.customer_reply: Thanks for reporting the duplicate fulfilment tasks. To help us investigate, could you share a redacted example with the event ID, delivery attempt times and the related task IDs? Please do not include signing secrets or access tokens. Could you also confirm whether this affects only these three orders? We can then compare delivery acknowledgements with the receiving system's processing records.

title: CSV preview shows fewer accepted records
description: A fictional stock team uploaded a CSV containing 120 lines. The preview accepted 112 records and marked five lines invalid plus three duplicate identifiers. The team believes eight records have disappeared. The source file has not been changed and the import has not been committed.

draft.summary: The reported difference between 120 source lines and 112 accepted records matches the five invalid and three duplicate lines. Their treatment and identifier rules still need confirmation before an import is committed.

observations.statement: The preview reports 112 accepted, five invalid and three duplicate lines; the import is not committed.
Accepted, invalid and duplicate rows should be counted separately and checked against the original source.

checks.action: Compare the original file headers and identifier fields with the preview's validation messages.
checks.reason: This can explain the five invalid lines without changing the original file.

checks.action: Confirm the duplicate-identifier rule and reconcile all three preview counts to the source total.
checks.reason: Duplicate lines must not silently increase accepted totals or be mistaken for unexplained loss.

missing_information: Which validation messages are shown for the five invalid lines?
Are duplicate identifiers expected in the source format?
draft.customer_reply: Thanks for flagging the record difference. The preview counts currently account for all 120 lines, including five invalid and three duplicate lines. Could you share the column names and redacted validation messages so we can check how those lines are being classified? Please retain the original file and leave the import uncommitted while the preview is reviewed.

title: One team member receives a 403 on an export
description: A fictional team member can sign in and view reports but receives HTTP 403 when requesting an export. Another team member can export the same report. A fresh sign-in did not change the result. No token values or passwords have been included, and the user's export permission has not yet been checked.

draft.summary: The export is denied for one authenticated team member while report viewing works. The 403 response and differing behaviour warrant a permission/scope check; the report does not establish the underlying configuration.

observations.statement: Viewing works, but the export returns 403 for one user even after a fresh sign-in.
A 403 may indicate insufficient permissions for an authenticated request.

checks.action: Compare the affected user's export permission and requested scope with the documented requirements, without sharing token values.
checks.reason: The denied operation may require permissions that viewing does not.

checks.action: Record the exact export operation, UTC timestamp and redacted request ID for escalation.
checks.reason: A reproducible, scoped report helps a human investigate the access mismatch.

missing_information: Does the affected user have the required export permission?
What redacted request ID and timestamp accompany the failed export?
draft.customer_reply: Thanks for the details. Because sign-in and report viewing work while the export returns 403, could your administrator confirm whether your account has the required export permission? Please share only the export time and a redacted request ID, not passwords or token values. These details will help us investigate the difference between viewing and exporting.
